name: Long Island Sound Futures Fund
summary: Grants for habitat restoration, water quality, resilience and community outreach projects in the Long Island Sound watershed of Connecticut and New York, with some work eligible across neighbouring states.

eligibility.rule: Applicant is not a U.S. federal agency, business, or unincorporated individual
Lies in the Long Island Sound watershed, in the part its project type allows
Project is not a research project
Terrestrial invasive control has an existing or planned long-term operations and maintenance plan
Project is not stand-alone control of large monoculture common reed meadows
Ends within 24 months of award (36 for education or large complex work)

documents: Data Collection Information Form, if proposing to collect data
Statement of Litigation, unless a government applicant
Board of Trustees or Directors list, or statement that none exists
GAAP audited financial statements, unless current valid information is already on file
IRS Form 990, unless current valid information is already on file
Single Audit, unless current valid information is already on file

status.quote: Long Island Sound Futures Fund 2026 Request for Proposals - CLOSED

deadline.quote: Full Proposal Due Date May 19th, 2026, 11:59 PM, EDT

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, state government agencies, local government, municipal government, Tribal Governments and Organizations, and educational institutions

geography.quote: All proposed projects must be within the Long Island Sound Watershed boundary as shown in Figure 2.

access.quote: All application materials must be submitted online through National Fish and Wildlife Foundation's Easygrants system.

co_finance_required.quote: Projects must have a minimum match of 0.5:1 non-federal cash or in-kind contributions.

eligibility.quote: Ineligible applicants include U.S. Federal government agencies, businesses, and unincorporated individuals
All proposed projects must be within the Long Island Sound Watershed boundary as shown in Figure 2. Project eligibility is also limited by geography depending on the project type.
Research projects. Consider the LIS Partnership Research Grant Program.
Efforts to treat or control terrestrial invasive plants without an existing or planned for long-term invasive control operations and maintenance plan
Proposals for stand-alone control of large meadows of monoculture common reed (Phragmites australis) are not eligible for funding

be completed within 24 months after notification of grant award. Project completion dates for projects may be adjusted to reflect the school year for educational projects. Education projects must be completed within 36 months after notification of grant award. Larger-scale complex implementation must be completed within 36 months after notification of the grant award.

co_finance.quote: Projects must have a minimum match of 0.5:1 non-federal cash or in-kind contributions.
